title: CLEAR Travel Tips: How to Prepare for a Destination Wedding
summary: Learn how to prepare for wedding travel with practical tips for flights, packing, the airport, and how to navigate delays with backup plans to help keep your wedding on track.
body_markdown:
Wedding travel can be stressful. Whether you're traveling for your own wedding, as a guest, or as part of the wedding party, even the smallest disruption can make your travel day more challenging.


While you can't control the weather or airline schedules, planning ahead can help you stay prepared if your itinerary changes so you can stay focused on the celebration ahead.


‍


## Build Flexibility into Your Travel Plans


One of the simplest ways to reduce the impact of travel delays is to avoid a last minute arrival. When booking your trip, try to arrive one or two days before the wedding and choose an early nonstop flight if you can. Early departures are often less affected by delays that build throughout the day, while nonstop flights reduce the risk of missed connections. It's also worth avoiding the final flight of the day when other options are available.


Building extra time into your schedule gives you more flexibility if your plans change, as well.


‍


## Keep Wedding Essentials with You


Keep the items you'll need most in your carry-on whenever possible. That includes your wedding dress or formal attire, wedding rings, marriage license or other important documents, and shoes & accessories if you have room. If your checked bag is delayed, you'll still have the essentials for the ceremony while the airline works to locate your luggage.


If you're bringing your wedding gown onboard, read our guide to[Flying With a Wedding Dress](https://www.clearme.com/blog/travel-tips-flying-with-wedding-dress) for tips on packing and transporting it safely.


‍


## Stay Ahead of Flight Changes


Checking your itinerary before heading to the airport gives you more time to adjust if your flight is affected. Before you travel, have your boarding pass ready and check the[weather](https://www.weather.gov/) at both your departure and arrival airports.


Add your flight in the[CLEAR App](https://www.clearme.com/clear-mobile-app) to know exactly when to leave, based on traffic, airport conditions, and real-time travel day updates. It's also worth reviewing your airline's rebooking options and familiarizing yourself with the U.S. Department of Transportation's Airline Cancellation and Delay[Dashboard](https://www.transportation.gov/airconsumer/airline-cancellation-delay-dashboard) , which compares the commitments airlines make to passengers during controllable delays and cancellations.


‍


## Create a Simple Backup Plan


Taking a few minutes to prepare before your trip can make it easier to respond if your plans change. Share your itinerary with your partner or members of the wedding party, save your venue, hotel, and vendor contact information, and keep digital copies of important documents. If you're working with a tight schedule, identify alternative flights or nearby airports ahead of time.


If severe weather or another disruption affects your trip, having those options ready can save valuable time.

‍


## Give Yourself Extra Time at the Airport


Traffic, parking, and busy travel days can all add extra time before your flight. Giving yourself some buffer time means you won't have to rush if one part of your trip takes longer than expected.
